feature: Ask puts a copy's words in the copy
summary: When a document has its own component, Ask places copies that say their own words, instead of laying new text over them. A component name Ask gets wrong is now caught while it plans, so it can correct itself. The held-out layout score on the final build is 66.3, against a bar of 30.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default, a blank 1440 x 900 canvas, the built-in model.

try.do: On a blank canvas, drag a Button from the Library's Comps tab onto the picture.
Click Ask in the title bar, type 'Add three more of the Button component in a row under it, saying Starter, Pro and Team' and press Send.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick one of the new buttons and read its row in Layers: it says Copy, and its own word is on it.
On a new blank canvas, ask 'Make a pricing section on brand' and wait for the row in the Agent group, four to six minutes on this Mac.
try.shotNote: The final build. Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Check that the three cards sit in one even row, with every word inside its card.
Press Command Z once: the whole section is gone.

evaluate: Does the pricing section look like a person laid it out, or would you nudge something first?
On a blank canvas Ask draws its cards as shapes with separate words, because starters are kept from it. Is that right, or should it place Library Cards?
Is four to six minutes for a pricing section something you would wait for?
rough: No mock covers the layout Ask makes: agent-generate-wt.html gives only the request.

Two of four pricing tries on the final build got no first answer from the model, at 300 s and at 420 s, and made nothing. The other two finished in 210 s and 347 s. I do not know why; memory was healthy afterwards. Folded into task ask-s-first-answer-after-its-model-loads-comes-i.
Asked for 'Card starter components' on a blank canvas, Ask draws shapes instead, because starters are kept from it. The copy words were seen working live with a Button only, not a Card.

When steps fail as a plan runs, Ask still says nothing about them: three failed copies left two plans' words on white with no message. That is task when-ask-stops-part-way-it-says-so-and-one-refus; the name check stops this one way of getting there.
The Most popular pill sits left of its card's middle in the final picture, and its words count as overlapping the card, as a badge across an edge does.
The pricing case scores 61.4, against 67.9 on 2026-10-24. The rules mark it down for eight type sizes, which this work does not touch.
The cause of the layout drop rests on totals from past runs, not a fresh same-code comparison. The layout group is only three cases, so one case moves it by a third.
